name: Bonsai 27B
tagline: A 27B model pruned down to 3.9GB — small enough to live in your pocket
description: PrismML compresses Qwen3.6-27B to extremes: a ternary build ({−1, 0, +1}, 1.71 bits/weight, 5.9GB) keeping 94.6% of FP16 quality across 15 benchmarks, and a 1-bit build (1.125 bits/weight, 3.9GB) keeping 89.5% — running ~11 tok/s on an iPhone 17 Pro Max. Ships as GGUF for llama.cpp and MLX for Apple Silicon, with forked runtimes on GitHub.
why: The first credible 27B-class model that fits on a phone moves the local-AI frontier from 'gaming laptop' to 'thing already in your pocket' — fully offline, no telemetry, and Apache-2.0 end to end, inherited cleanly from its Apache base.
useCases: On-device assistants on phones with ~6GB free memory
Offline laptop inference without a discrete GPU
audience: Local-AI enthusiasts, mobile developers, quantization researchers

setup.requirements: 1-bit build needs ~6GB free memory (iOS-capable); ternary wants ~8GB; runs via PrismML's llama.cpp and MLX forks

license.code: Apache-2.0 (PrismML runtime forks and demo repo)
license.notes: Weights repos are tagged Apache-2.0, consistent with the Apache-2.0 Qwen3.6-27B base they derive from; the modified llama.cpp/MLX runtimes are forks of Apache/MIT projects. No riders found in the cards.

tally.stars: ~34k HF downloads/mo on the 1-bit MLX build alone

limitations: The quality retention is uneven — vision tasks drop hardest (to ~60–65% of baseline), the 1-bit build's losses are real in the tails, and you're tied to PrismML's forked runtimes until upstream support lands.
take: Colibri streams a 744B model off a hard drive; Bonsai shrinks a 27B into a phone. Two opposite bets, one thesis: the hardware you own is enough.
